title: Forces & Motion
description: Newton's laws, speed, velocity, acceleration, and balanced/unbalanced forces.

notes.heading: Speed, Velocity, Acceleration
notes.body: Speed = distance ÷ time (m/s). Velocity = speed with direction (vector). Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time (m/s²). Distance-time graphs: slope = speed. Velocity-time graphs: slope = acceleration, area under = distance.

notes.heading: Newton's Three Laws
notes.body: 1st: Object stays at rest or constant velocity unless acted on by a net force. 2nd: F = ma (force = mass × acceleration). 3rd: For every action, equal and opposite reaction.

notes.heading: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
notes.body: Balanced forces → zero net force → object stays still or constant velocity. Unbalanced forces → net force → acceleration. Weight W = mg (g ≈ 10 m/s² on Earth). Friction, air resistance, and normal force are common forces.

flashcards.definition: Distance per unit time: speed = distance ÷ time.
Rate of change of velocity: a = Δv ÷ t (m/s²).
The single force with the same effect as all individual forces combined.

questions.stem: Car travels 150 m in 10 s. Average speed?
Skydiver falling at constant speed. Forces are:
questions.explanation: Constant speed → zero acceleration → forces balanced (Newton's 1st law).

questions.stem: Rocket expels gas downward. Rocket goes:
questions.explanation: Newton's 3rd law: gas pushes down, rocket pushes up.
